correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary sequence of nonnegative curvatures bounded by L, assuming divergent variation forces eventual normalized steps in [0,1]. Telescoping descent makes the sum of squared gradients divided by adaptive weights finite; the bound w_n<=C+2sqrt(sum g_j^2) and the sqrt-telescoping lower bound contradict any divergent sum g_j^2. The resulting finite variation plus infinitely many Bernoulli zero-to-active transitions forces strict terminal stability; the strong law and scalar product yield almost-sure exponential contraction and the exact rate. Finite rational/trajectory tests verify implementation but not the infinite limit.
